artists.biography: The Supernaturals were a five-piece guitar based pop band from Glasgow, Scotland. Fronted by singer-songwriter James McColl, they signed to Parlophone in 1996, and had a string of singles which were taken from their three albums and four EPs. Other members included Mark Guthrie, Derek McManus and Ken McAlpine. The band's best known songs ("Smile" and "I Wasn't Built To Get Up") were featured prominently in a series of television advertisements. In total they scored five Top 40 entries in the UK Singles Chart.

It Doesn't Matter Anymore" is the debut studio album by Scottish rock band The Supernaturals, originally released in 1997 on Parlophone/Food Records. The album is rooted in the Britpop and indie rock movements of the mid-1990s, characterized by melodic guitar-driven songs, catchy hooks, and a distinctly British sensibility. Its sound blends upbeat, anthemic tracks with introspective moments, showcasing the band's knack for accessible songwriting and memorable choruses.

As the band's first full-length release, "It Doesn't Matter Anymore" established The Supernaturals as a notable presence in the UK rock scene. The album reached number 9 on the UK Albums Chart and produced four top 40 singles, including the critically acclaimed "Smile," which was nominated for an Ivor Novello Award in 1998. Several tracks from the album also appeared on prominent Britpop compilations, further cementing its place in the era's musical landscape. While the band's subsequent releases did not achieve the same level of commercial success, "It Doesn't Matter Anymore" remains a well-regarded example of 1990s British indie rock.
